summary.plain: The ADMX detector uses a powerful magnet and a supercooled tunable metal cavity to try to convert dark-matter axions into faint microwave signals, which are then amplified and measured.
summary.technical: Tunable copper-plated microwave cavity haloscope inside a superconducting solenoid, cooled by a dilution refrigerator to ~90 mK and read out with near-quantum-limited amplifiers, at CENPA (University of Washington).

technology.value: Microwave-cavity haloscope: a tunable, cylindrical copper-plated resonant cavity inside a large superconducting solenoid magnet, read out through a dilution refrigerator and a near-quantum-limited (Josephson parametric / SQUID) amplifier chain.
